fragment_extraction.mockable_seam_decision: Per analysis.md's unit-test strategy: this project uses fixture-based tests, NOT mocks. The C original never abstracted FILE*/HashTable behind an interface, and both are cheap/local/deterministic (no network, DB, or clock), so no mock trait is introduced. The mockable 'seam' for io/parser is the real filesystem via std::env::temp_dir()-rooted temp files created/cleaned up per test; the seam for hash_table/reducer/typechecker is direct construction of small in-memory AstNode/HashTable/TypeEnv fixtures. This mirrors the Makefile's original per-module, non-mocked test-binary structure.

implementation_plan.title: common: AstNode model and string rendering
implementation_plan.goal: Implement common.rs: Default for AstNode (empty-VAR sentinel), set_verbose/print_verbose/print_ast_verbose, error(), format(), append_to_buffer, append_ast_to_buffer, ast_to_string -- exact C textual contract per node type.
steps_part_a: Implement `impl Default for AstNode` as an empty VAR node (name="", type_="").
Implement set_verbose (module-level mutable bool, e.g. AtomicBool or thread-unsafe static with unsafe accessor to mirror C's static bool) and print_verbose/print_ast_verbose gated on it.
Implement error() to eprintln! the C-style message then std::process::exit(1).
Implement format() as a thin wrapper over std::fmt::format(args) (fmt already provided by caller via format_args!).
Implement append_to_buffer/append_ast_to_buffer/ast_to_string matching the exact C string shape per AstNodeType (fragments: common.c:append_ast_to_buffer switch arms).
steps_part_b: Un-ignore and implement common.rs tests: build hand-made VAR/LAMBDA_EXPR/APPLICATION AstNode fixtures and assert exact ast_to_string output including trailing spaces.
Implement test_default_ast_node_is_empty_var_sentinel asserting the Default sentinel renders as the empty-name VAR string.

implementation_plan.title: hash_table: insert/search/table_exists/delete
implementation_plan.goal: Implement hash_table.rs on HashMap<String, common::AstNode>: hash() (djb2 mod HASH_TABLE_SIZE), createHashTable/destroyHashTable, insert/search/table_exists/delete with Default-sentinel-as-None search semantics.
steps_part_a: Implement hash() as a faithful djb2 port using wrapping arithmetic (u32/u64 wrapping_mul/wrapping_add) then `% HASH_TABLE_SIZE as u32`.
Implement HashTable::new/createHashTable as HashMap::new() wrappers; destroyHashTable as a no-op consuming its argument (Drop handles the rest).
Implement insert to HashMap::insert(key.to_string(), value).

Implement search to return None both when the key is absent AND when the stored value equals AstNode::default() (compare via common::ast_to_string or a dedicated is_default check), mirroring C's NULL-valued bucket entries.
Implement table_exists as self.table.contains_key(key) (documented HashMap-driven simplification of C's bucket-based check).
Implement delete as self.table.remove(key); discard result.
steps_part_b: Un-ignore hash_table.rs tests: insert+search round trip, default-sentinel search returns None, table_exists true/false, delete then search None, hash() bounded/deterministic.
implementation_plan.gate: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib -- hash_table:: passes

implementation_plan.title: io: file wrappers
implementation_plan.goal: Implement io.rs: create_file/get_file/write_to_file/delete_file/close_file returning io::Result<_> via ?, and next() as a byte-read + cursor-advance (fgetc-equivalent).
steps_part_a: Implement create_file via OpenOptions::new().write(true).create(true).truncate(true).open(path)?.
Implement get_file via File::open/OpenOptions per the requested mode string (e.g. "r" -> read, "w" -> write/create).
Implement write_to_file via file.write_all(content.as_bytes())? then seek back to start (rewind-equivalent).
Implement delete_file via std::fs::remove_file(path)?.
Implement close_file as drop(file); Ok(()) (Rust closes files on drop; return Ok to preserve the Result signature).
Implement next() by reading exactly one byte via Read::read, returning the EOF sentinel char on 0 bytes read, else the byte cast to char (mirrors fgetc's char cast).
steps_part_b: Un-ignore io.rs tests: create+write+get+read-back round trip using std::env::temp_dir()-rooted paths (cleaned up at test end); delete_file then get_file errors; next() reads one byte and advances the cursor.
implementation_plan.gate: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib -- io:: passes

implementation_plan.title: config: options parsing
implementation_plan.goal: Implement config.rs: trim() (isspace-bounded), get_config_type(), parse_config() (split on first '='), get_config_from_file() (line-by-line via BufRead, opening the referenced lambda file through io::get_file, panicking on fatal errors).
steps_part_a: Implement trim() in-place on &mut String, reproducing C's isspace-bounded start/end scan and off-by-one edge behavior for all-whitespace/single-char strings.

Implement get_config_type() matching "file"/"step_by_step_reduction"/"reduction_order" to their variants, else CONFIG_ERROR (matches C's error()-then-CONFIG_ERROR fallthrough behavior, invoked but non-fatal from the Rust side unless the caller panics).
Implement parse_config() to split line on the first '=' via splitn(2, '='), trim both halves into key/value.

Implement get_config_from_file() to open config::CONFIG_PATH via io::get_file, read lines with BufRead::lines(), call parse_config/get_config_type per line, open the referenced lambda file via io::get_file, and .expect()/panic! on any fatal condition (missing file=, unrecognized key, bad reduction_order value) exactly where C called error().
steps_part_b: Un-ignore config.rs tests for trim/get_config_type/parse_config as pure-string tests (no I/O needed for these three).
implementation_plan.gate: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib -- config:: passes

implementation_plan.title: typechecker: structural type checking
implementation_plan.goal: Implement typechecker.rs: Type/TypeEnv, assert_, typecheck() (VAR/APPLICATION/LAMBDA_EXPR, preserving the non-arrow-codomain limitation on APPLICATION), type_equal, get_type_from_expr, create_type/parse_function_type, expr_type_equal, add_to_env, lookup_type.
steps_part_a: Implement assert_() to panic!("{}", error_msg) when expr is false (mirrors C's assert_ fatal behavior).

Implement typecheck() for VAR (lookup_type/get_type_from_expr), APPLICATION (assert type_equal of function/argument types, return the function's own Type unchanged -- do NOT compute a codomain), and LAMBDA_EXPR (recursively typecheck body under an extended env, build the arrow-shaped Type via create_type/parse_function_type).
Implement type_equal/expr_type_equal as string-equality on the type_/return_type fields, matching C's NULL-vs-"" asymmetry handling ("" == absent).
Implement get_type_from_expr/create_type/parse_function_type per the C field extraction and '->'-split parsing.
Implement add_to_env(env: &mut Option<Box<TypeEnv>>, type_: Type) by prepending a new TypeEnv node (mirrors C's TypeEnv** insertion).
Implement lookup_type() by walking the Option<Box<TypeEnv>> chain matching on the AstNode's variable name.
steps_part_b: Un-ignore typechecker.rs tests: VAR/LAMBDA_EXPR typecheck success cases, type_equal string comparisons, add_to_env+lookup_type round trip.
implementation_plan.gate: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib -- typechecker:: passes

implementation_plan.title: parser: lexer and recursive-descent grammar
implementation_plan.goal: Implement parser.rs on top of common and hash_table: parse_token, is_variable, peek/peek_print (EOF-sentinel pushback via Seek), consume/expect (fatal on mismatch), create_variable/create_application/create_lambda, alpha_convert (atomic counter), is_used, parse_space_chars, the grammar functions, and free_ast.
steps_part_a: Implement parse_token() as an exact char->tokens_t match (parens, '@'->LAMBDA, '.'->DOT, whitespace/newline/'='/'"'/':' cases, is_variable(c)->VARIABLE, else ERROR).
Implement is_variable() to accept '_' plus ASCII letters (a-z, A-Z) only.
Implement peek()/peek_print() via Read::read of one byte + Seek::seek(SeekFrom::Current(-1)) pushback, returning the EOF sentinel char on 0 bytes read.
Implement consume()/expect() to call peek/read the next token, exit(1)/panic with the C's fatal message shape on mismatch.
Implement create_variable/create_application/create_lambda as plain AstNode constructors.
Implement alpha_convert() using a module-level AtomicU32 counter, producing "<old>_<n>" and incrementing.
Implement is_used() via hash_table::HashTable::table_exists.
Implement parse_space_chars() to consume whitespace/newline tokens via peek/consume in a loop.

Implement the grammar functions parse_lambda/parse_expression/parse_import/parse_definition/parse_type_definition/parse_type/parse_variable per the C recursive-descent structure, threading the HashTable for definitions/types/bound-variable tracking.
Implement free_ast() as a no-op (or explicit drop of node's owned children) since Rust's ownership already frees the tree; keep the signature for contract parity.
steps_part_b: Un-ignore parser.rs tests: parse_token table-driven assertions, is_variable boundary cases ('_' plus letters vs digits/symbols), alpha_convert monotonic suffix assertions across repeated calls, and an end-to-end parse_expression fixture (write a small lambda expr string to a temp file, parse, assert via common::ast_to_string).
implementation_plan.gate: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib -- parser:: passes

implementation_plan.title: reducer: beta/eta reduction engine
implementation_plan.goal: Implement reducer.rs on top of common, hash_table, parser, config: set_reduction_order/print_reduction_order, reduce(), expand_definitions() (in-place, panics if a definition is absent), replace() (in-place renaming), reduce_ast() (applicative vs normal exactly as coded), substitute(), and deepcopy*.
steps_part_a: Implement set_reduction_order/print_reduction_order using a module-level mutable reduction_order_t state (mirrors C's file-scope variable) plus printing its name.
Implement deepcopy/deepcopy_application/deepcopy_lambda_expr/deepcopy_var as owned recursive tree-cloning helpers (used by substitute to avoid aliasing).

Implement substitute() to recursively rebuild an owned AstNode replacing free occurrences of `variable` with a deepcopy of `replacement`, exactly matching C's (non-alpha-safe-at-substitution-time) logic.

Implement reduce_ast() to branch on the current reduction_order: applicative reduces function and argument fully then beta-reduces and returns the substitution directly; normal reduces lazily and recurses into reduce_ast again on the result -- match the C control flow exactly, not the comments.

Implement expand_definitions() as in-place &mut AstNode mutation: for DEFINITION nodes, look up the name in `table` and panic!() (mirroring HANDLE_NULL) if absent, else overwrite the node's union/type; recurse into children.
Implement replace() as in-place bound-variable renaming through a subtree (used post alpha_convert).
Implement reduce() to call expand_definitions then reduce_ast, with optional verbose tracing via common::print_ast_verbose.
steps_part_b: Un-ignore reducer.rs tests: build small typed lambda ASTs in-memory, assert reduce_ast output (compared via common::ast_to_string) for both APPLICATIVE and NORMAL order, substitute() free-variable replacement, expand_definitions() rewriting a DEFINITION node from a populated HashTable, and deepcopy() producing a structurally-identical but independently-owned tree.
implementation_plan.gate: cargo build succeeds; cargo test --lib -- reducer:: passes
